design_rules.title: Finished end at an open end, filler at a wall
design_rules.says: An applied end panel matching the doors goes on any cabinet end with no wall and no cabinet beside it. A filler goes at a wall end.

design_rules.title: Shelves evenly spaced, no opening under 6"
design_rules.says: Adjustable shelves in a space are spaced evenly, and no opening between them may be less than 6".

design_rules.title: Door sizes and splits
design_rules.says: 1/16" from each outside edge; each door of a pair is 1/8" less than half the cabinet; one door up to 20" wide, then a pair; one door up to 48" tall, then two stacked. Under a countertop the door top is 1/4" down from the cabinet top; otherwise flush.

design_rules.title: Dividing a run into cabinets
design_rules.says: The run length is fixed. Each end gives up 3/4" to a filler (at a wall) or an applied finished end (open end). The rest is divided into cabinets by outside width on 1/16" steps, with the aims PREF-001 to PREF-004. Making one cabinet wider makes the others narrower.

design_rules.title: Corners: the longest run takes the corner
design_rules.says: The longest run goes to the end of its wall; the run on the next wall stops about 10" short of its fronts, with an end panel. No corner cabinet.
design_rules.applies_when: Closet cabinet runs facing each other, while a run is being dragged in the wall and cabinet layout step

design_rules.title: Upgrade: 1 1/2" fillers and finished ends
design_rules.says: An optional room-wide upgrade makes every filler and finished end 1 1/2" thick (one sheet-good panel, not solid wood). Each such run end then sets aside 1 1/2" instead of 3/4".

design_rules.title: Crown moulding sets the gap above the cabinets
design_rules.says: With a crown, the cabinet top is exactly the crown's size below the ceiling (height set from the ceiling down). With no crown, any height, but never closer than 1" to the ceiling. Placeholder crowns: 2", 3", 4", 5", 6".

design_rules.title: Fronts on one cabinet are grain-matched
design_rules.says: The fronts of one cabinet are always cut from grain-matched, continuous sections of the sheet, for every grained or patterned material. "Non-negotiable."

design_rules.title: Stone countertop drawings show intent only
design_rules.says: The stone templater measures on site. Our countertop drawings show overall sizes, finished, unfinished and wall edges, and where fixtures and appliances go. They don't replace the field template.

design_rules.title: Runs never occupy the same floor
design_rules.says: Each run claims its length along the wall plus its depth and room for fronts and handles. No other run may enter that space. Facing runs in a galley too narrow for both are reported, not overlapped.

design_rules.title: A run stays inside its wall
design_rules.says: A run is never longer than its wall allows. A room edit that shortens a wall shortens its runs, and the screen says so.

design_rules.title: Boxes stand gable to gable
design_rules.says: In a row each cabinet starts exactly where the one before it ends. With the fillers and end panels, the cabinets fill the run exactly.

design_rules.title: Dishwasher right beside the sink base
design_rules.says: The dishwasher and the sink base must touch. No filler or corner between them (the dishwasher drains into the sink's drain).

design_rules.title: A cabinet over the fridge is centred on the fridge
design_rules.says: A cabinet over a fridge is perfectly centred on the fridge.
design_rules.applies_when: A cabinet sits over a fridge

design_rules.title: Whatever is over a cooktop is centred on it
design_rules.says: A hood fan, millwork hood or cabinet over a cooktop or range is centred on it. When the space over it is left open, the uppers either side are sized so the gap between them is centred on the cooktop. The gap's width comes from the code and the installation manual (the stricter decides), not a fixed 2" a side.

design_rules.title: 30" clear above the cooking surface
design_rules.says: Combustible cabinetry above a cooktop or range is at least 30" above the cooking surface. The building code's reductions and its exemptions for hoods and microwaves are not verified.
design_rules.applies_when: Cabinetry above a cooktop or range, Manitoba

design_rules.title: Protection of combustibles beside a cooktop
design_rules.says: From research, NOT VERIFIED: combustible finishes or cabinets within about 450 mm of the cooktop are protected above element level. No value is to be used until the code text is read.

design_rules.title: Appliance and fixture specs confirmed before sign-off
design_rules.says: Placeholder appliances are fine while designing. Sign-off and sending to production wait until every appliance's and fixture's specs are confirmed and the cabinetry meets their installation requirements.

design_rules.title: Countertop into an appliance opening: at most 1/4", equal both sides
design_rules.says: Where a countertop ends at an appliance or fixture opening, it projects 0 to 1/4" from each side, never more, and the two sides are exactly equal. The usual 1" overhang does not apply there. Example: a 31" opening for a slide-in range gives a 30 1/2" counter opening.

design_rules.title: Verified site measurements before sign-off
design_rules.says: A design may use preliminary measurements, and a quote may use the homeowner's or a blueprint's. Sign-off and production need verified site measurements, recording who verified them and when (us, a contractor, the designer or the homeowner).

design_rules.title: Anything that opens opens without hitting anything
design_rules.says: Doors, drawers, roll-outs, corner hardware and appliance doors complete their movement without hitting cabinetry, handles, walls, appliances, room doors or each other. Handles count. No clearance distance is invented: it comes from the real hardware and appliance.

design_rules.title: Known site conditions are constraints
design_rules.says: Walls, bump-outs, columns, doors, windows, soffits, plumbing, electrical, HVAC and hood ducts that affect fit or use are constraints when known.

design_rules.title: Smallest cabinet widths
design_rules.says: By outside width: an upper at least 8"; a base with only doors at least 8"; a cabinet with drawers at least 12".

design_rules.title: No cabinet wider than 42"
design_rules.says: A cabinet is never more than 42" wide. Up to 38" one cabinet is preferred to two (PREF-025).

design_rules.title: Pot-lid organiser
design_rules.says: A dedicated pot-lid organiser is an optional upgrade, never added automatically.

design_rules.title: Pull-out ironing board
design_rules.says: Useful but optional, never added automatically.

design_rules.title: Cabinets 24" to 32" wide
design_rules.says: When a run is divided into cabinets, make as many as possible 24" to 32" wide. The ideal for looks and for sheet yield.

design_rules.title: Few cabinets over 36"
design_rules.says: As few cabinets as possible over 36" wide. Loses to PREF-025 up to 38".

design_rules.title: Avoid cabinets under 12"
design_rules.says: Avoid cabinets narrower than 12". An aim, not a limit (the limits are HARD-015).

design_rules.title: Fairly symmetrical runs
design_rules.says: Cabinet widths across a run look balanced, but cabinet size comes first: 80" of cabinets is 32 + 32 + 16, not three of 26 5/8. A 90" run is two 3/4" fillers and three 29 1/2" cabinets. ASSUMED order of trying (read from those examples): equal cabinets if they land in 24–32"; then full 32s plus one; then the most even split, wider ones at both ends; an odd one at the right end.

design_rules.title: Shoe and boot shelf spacing
design_rules.says: Flat shoe shelves 8" apart, the first 7" up; boots 16".

design_rules.title: A four-drawer bank near the sink and dishwasher
design_rules.says: A bank of four drawers should be close to the sink cabinet and dishwasher.

design_rules.title: One or two four-drawer banks beside the cooktop
design_rules.says: At least one, ideally two, four-drawer banks for pots and pans right beside the cooking appliance. Closer is better. Drawers, not deep shelves behind doors.

design_rules.title: Countertop overhangs 1"
design_rules.says: Counters overhang 1" past a finished end and 1" past the face of a door or drawer front. Not at an appliance opening (HARD-011).

design_rules.title: The cabinet over the fridge lines up with the fridge panel
design_rules.says: The cabinet over a fridge is deep enough that its door face is flush with the front of the fridge panel beside it.

design_rules.title: Walkways 42" to 48"
design_rules.says: Under 36": breaks a very strong minimum. 36" to 42": possible, below preferred. 42" to 48": preferred. Over 48": breaks a very strong maximum. Measured from the countertop edge. The two minimums also apply between cabinets and a bare wall (owner, 2026-11-09).

design_rules.title: Islands line up with nearby runs
design_rules.says: Islands are sized and placed to line up with other runs. When an island's end is within 5" of lining up with a wall run's end, they line up exactly ("like snapping"), by resizing and placing cabinets.

design_rules.title: An island sink and a back-wall range line up exactly
design_rules.says: An island sink and a back-wall range are lined up exactly: 100% in line, not only when they are roughly in line.

design_rules.title: A roughly centred island fixture is centred exactly
design_rules.says: A sink or cooktop roughly centred on an island is centred exactly.
design_rules.strength: extremely strong, "almost a hard constraint", but not hard

design_rules.title: Solve the fixed things first, then share out the rest
design_rules.says: 1 set the run's ends; 2 set aside fillers and end panels; 3 lock confirmed appliance and fixture openings; 4 lock cabinets with deliberate widths; 5 share the remaining space; 6 recheck the total.

design_rules.title: Acceptable cabinet widths 12" to 36"
design_rules.says: 12–36" is acceptable; 24–32" is ideal (PREF-001).

design_rules.title: Ideal door width 14" to 16"
design_rules.says: Each visible door: ideal 14–16"; backup 12–14" and 16–20". Drawer fronts have no ideal width (the cabinet width decides). A 30" two-door cabinet is judged on its two 14 7/8" doors.

design_rules.title: Drawer and front lines carry across neighbours
design_rules.says: Lines between drawer fronts continue across neighbouring drawer banks, and prominent front lines (the top of a door and the drawer beside it) continue across neighbouring bases. Random changes score worse unless function or a deliberate composition explains them.

design_rules.title: Equal widths either side of a focal point
design_rules.says: Around a range, hood, over-range cabinet, sink, major window, niche or feature cabinet, the two cabinets immediately either side are equal widths where function allows. 18 | 36 HOOD | 18 beats 15 | 36 HOOD | 21.

design_rules.title: Consistent top and bottom lines; deliberate steps
design_rules.says: A tall cabinet beside uppers shares their top line. Uppers in one run keep a consistent top, bottom or crown line. Where heights change, the change looks deliberate (a hierarchy, a repeated step, a focal composition), not accidental.

design_rules.title: Repeated widths make rhythm; random one-offs are penalised
design_rules.says: Within one area, use a small deliberate set of widths (not every cabinet equal). 24 | 30 | 24 | 30 | 24 beats 18 | 27 | 21 | 33 | 16 | 24. A width that function needs is never refused.

design_rules.title: Style decides how many divisions
design_rules.says: Calm or contemporary designs suit fewer, wider fronts. Traditional or detailed designs can suit more, smaller divisions.

design_rules.title: Sink centred under a window; balance around a focal window
design_rules.says: When a sink and window are nearly aligned and function allows, the sink centres under the window. Cabinetry either side of a focal window is balanced. Local to the window; not every sink goes under every window.

design_rules.title: Narrow doors beside a cooktop or sink hinge away from it
design_rules.says: Narrow single-door cabinets right beside the cooktop or sink open away from it, because the cook stands there. In 28 | 14 | 36 | 14 | 28 the left 14 hinges left, the right 14 hinges right. Never overrides HARD-013.
design_rules.strength: very strong beside a cooktop or sink; a weaker bonus beside prep areas; not hard

design_rules.title: Up to 38", one cabinet beats two narrow ones
design_rules.says: Where the space could be one cabinet up to about 38" or two of half that, one is better. Beats PREF-002 up to 38". Never over 42" (HARD-016).

design_rules.title: Drawers rather than doors for everyday base storage
design_rules.says: Full-extension drawer bases are preferred to doors with shelves for kitchens, and vanities where plumbing allows. Except sinks, equipment, specialty cabinets, or where a door is genuinely better.

design_rules.title: A cutlery drawer and a separate utensil drawer
design_rules.says: One drawer for flatware with a cutlery insert, and a separate drawer for cooking utensils. Both by default in a full kitchen.

design_rules.title: Cutlery and everyday dishes near the dishwasher
design_rules.says: What is put away from the dishwasher, above all cutlery, goes near the dishwasher and cleanup zone.

design_rules.title: Vertical tray storage, over the fridge by default
design_rules.says: Vertical dividers for baking sheets, cutting boards and trays, by default in the cabinet over the fridge when it can hold them.
design_rules.strength: default; its place is a strong default

design_rules.title: Concealed garbage and recycling between sink and prep
design_rules.says: An integrated waste and recycling pull-out, placed to serve both prep and the sink.
design_rules.strength: default; its place is very strong

design_rules.title: Pull-outs inside tall pantry cabinets
design_rules.says: Tall pantry cabinets get internal pull-out drawers or trays rather than deep fixed shelves.

design_rules.title: Organised spice storage by default
design_rules.says: A dedicated spice solution near the cooking zone. The system is undecided.

design_rules.title: A proper corner mechanism whenever a corner holds storage
design_rules.says: No deep blind corner with fixed shelves. If a corner holds storage it gets an access mechanism (carousel, corner pull-out or similar). Leaving the corner empty can be better.

design_rules.title: Laundry room basics
design_rules.says: A folding surface (very strong); somewhere to hang or air-dry clothes (strong); laundry products stored by the machines (strong).

design_rules.title: Mudroom basics
design_rules.says: A bench with shoe storage (very strong); small-item storage for keys, gloves and mail (strong); exposed hooks (moderate, never at the cost of the design).

design_rules.title: The recommended closet cabinet
design_rules.says: Top to bottom: a shelf over the hanging if there is room; open hanging with a rod; drawers at the bottom. Doors only if there is room to open them. A recommendation, not a rule.

design_rules.title: The stricter of the code and the installation manual decides
design_rules.says: When the building code and a manufacturer's installation manual give different clearances, follow the stricter.

design_rules.title: The installation guide beats the spec sheet
design_rules.says: When an appliance's spec sheet and installation guide disagree, use the installation guide.

design_rules.title: Clearances are measured from the finished outside
design_rules.says: Doors, fronts, finished panels, countertops, handles and appliances stand beyond the cabinet, so they decide the real clearance.

design_rules.title: Fillers and panels are real parts
design_rules.says: Fillers and end panels are their own items with their own space, not space hidden in a cabinet width.

design_rules.title: Walkways against alignment and centring: no fixed order
design_rules.says: When walkway width and alignment or centring pull against each other, the AI suggests the trade-off and explains it, and the designer decides. Narrowed by PRIN-013 for lining up.

design_rules.title: Near enough becomes exact
design_rules.says: When things that read as a pair or a shared line nearly match, close the gap. A small miss is worse than an exact match or a clearly deliberate offset. 17 7/8 | FOCAL | 18 1/8 becomes 18 | FOCAL | 18.

design_rules.title: Align the edges that matter, not every seam
design_rules.says: Uppers and bases may use different widths; their ordinary seams needn't line up. Related edges (run ends, appliance, window and tall-cabinet edges) should. Three 24" uppers over two 36" bases is fine.

design_rules.title: Some lines matter more than others
design_rules.says: Most important first: 1 focal appliance and hood centrelines; 2 window and sink axes; 3 the outer ends of a composition; 4 tall and upper top lines; 5 major drawer and front lines; 6 large panel and end lines; 7 ordinary seams.

design_rules.title: Judge the visible fronts, not just the cabinets
design_rules.says: Equal cabinet widths aren't enough; the visible doors and drawer fronts should balance and repeat. 18 | 24 | 36 FOCAL | 24 | 18 is symmetrical in cabinets; 14 | 28 | 36 FOCAL | 28 | 14 is better; 28 | 14 | 36 FOCAL | 14 | 28 is preferred (every door 13 7/8").

design_rules.title: Symmetry is local; deliberate asymmetry is fine
design_rules.says: A room can hold several compositions (a symmetrical range wall, an asymmetrical sink wall, a symmetrical island). A wider element may set a hierarchy on purpose. Asymmetry from function or design is fine; unexplained near-pairs are not.

design_rules.title: Function outranks decorative symmetry
design_rules.says: Don't chase symmetry at the cost of storage, appliance use, clearances, plumbing or the right cabinet type. Hard rules always win.

design_rules.title: Judge composition in elevation
design_rules.says: Front alignment, rhythm, heights and focal symmetry can only be judged in the wall (front) view, not the plan.

design_rules.title: Lining up beats a wider walkway, but not below 36"
design_rules.says: When lining up and walkway width can't both be met, lining up wins as long as the walkway stays over 36".

design_rules.title: Store things where they're used, sized to what they hold
design_rules.says: Reason from the task to what is stored to where it goes: cookware by the cooktop, cutlery by the dishwasher, spices by the cooking, garbage by prep and cleanup. Never add an insert just to fill leftover space.

design_rules.title: What counts as a default
design_rules.says: A feature is in a basic design by default only if an experienced designer would be surprised to see it missing. Nice-to-haves are optional and never added automatically.

design_rules.title: Separate the storage function from the product
design_rules.says: Rules name the function ("cutlery organisation", "corner access"); the catalog maps it to a product.

design_rules.title: Not defaults: vanity organiser drawer, hair-tool organiser, pull-out hamper, laundry sorting baskets
design_rules.says: None of these is added by default.
